close_reason: chat-server-local part (HashMap import) done in commit b265e06. The wider 13-positional-arg Message::new reshape (the type-design half in jmap-chat-types) is tracked as JMAP-x2gd.100 (canonical-template propagation: mail-types Email::new takes 6 args, chat-types drifted to 13).
description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/message.rs:456 — inside Message::new(...) constructor call:

    let mut msg = Message::new(
        Id::from("placeholder"),
        Id::from(create_id.as_str()),
        SenderId::Owner,
        chat_id,
        body,
        body_type,
        vec![],
        vec![],
        vec![],
        std::collections::HashMap::new(),    // <-- here
        sent_at,
        received_at,
        DeliveryState::Pending,
    );

The fully-qualified path `std::collections::HashMap::new()` is used inline in a positional constructor call. Two non-idiomatic concerns:

1. Inconsistent imports. The file does NOT `use std::collections::HashMap` at the top, yet it does `use std::collections::HashSet` at message.rs:8 — the asymmetry is local inconsistency. Either both should be top-level `use`d, or neither.

2. Twelve positional arguments to a constructor. `Message::new(...)` takes 13 positional args of which 4 are `vec![]` / `HashMap::new()` empty containers. This is exactly the call-site shape a builder pattern or a `Default`-and-struct-update pattern is designed to replace. The downstream four assignments at lines 462-467 (`msg.reply_to = ...; msg.thread_root_id = ...; msg.sender_expires_at = ...; msg.burn_on_read = ...`) reinforce the smell: the constructor takes 13 mandatory args, then the caller assigns 4 more optional fields imperatively. A struct-with-Default plus `Message { id, sender_id_msg, ..Default::default() }` would shrink this from 17 lines to 5 and make required-vs-optional structurally obvious.

This finding is about the message.rs handler — the wider Message::new shape lives in jmap-chat-types and would need a propagation bead there. But the *call-site* in message.rs is the part subject to this review.

What goes wrong if left:

- (1) is a clippy/style miss; a future contributor adding HashMap usage elsewhere will be unsure whether to import or fully-qualify.
- (2) is a real readability concern: positional constructors past 5-6 args lose call-site meaning. The reviewer cannot tell at a glance which `vec![]` is reactions, which is attachments, which is mentions. The risk is silently passing args to the wrong slot during refactors (the compiler won't catch it because all three Vec<_> slots accept the same `vec![]`).

Scope: P3 clippy for (1), P2 type-design for (2). Combined finding because they share a site and rewriting #2 dissolves #1.
title: message.rs Message::new call site: fully-qualified HashMap path + 13-positional-arg constructor
